current.text: Experts expect him to be last in Charlotte's center rotation and out of the rotation on many nights. Do not count on him.
Moussa Diabaté is projected to start at center. Kalkbrenner competes for backup center minutes with Diabaté, a first-round rookie and Kai Jones. Naz Reid and Grant Williams can also play the five.
Charlotte has a deep roster, so minutes for its reserve bigs are spread thin.
With a March 28 end, Charlotte plays 4, 3 and 4 games in our playoff weeks. The team has only 13 back-to-backs, the league minimum.
He is not worth a draft pick in a 12-team league.

durable.text: He is a strong shot blocker and the best rim protector among Charlotte's bigs.
He takes no threes. Charlotte does not let him shoot from the perimeter.
He finishes very efficiently around the rim, but his shot volume is low, so his FG% boost is modest.
He looks slow and gives little beyond rebounds and blocks. His points, assists and steals are low.

note: At 0 USD on both Yahoo and ESPN (rank 269 and 182), he is not one of the 144 players we draft. Last season he blocked 1.5 shots in 21.4 minutes, so his blocks are real, but experts expect him to be the last center in Charlotte's rotation. ESPN's 23.2-minute projection looks too high. Leave him on waivers and pick him up for blocks in a punt 3PM or punt STL build only if Diabaté gets hurt or he wins steady minutes early in the season.
